diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Therefore,
with the denominator going to $0$, we have $\kappa$ going to $\infty$
as $d = e+Vv$ approaches the boundary.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims the optima of the unconstrained κ-minimization over the open cone Rⁿ₊₊ are attained and attributes this to having a ratio of convex and concave functions over an open cone. Pseudoconvexity over an open set does not ensure attainment of a minimum. The remark then sketches a self-barrier argument (κ→∞ at the boundary of the normalized simplex) which would support attainment, but this argument asserts without proof that λ_min(d)→0 as d approaches the boundary ("with the denominator going to 0"). Although this limit claim is true (the limiting congruence D^{1/2}AD^{1/2} becomes rank-deficient when some dᵢ→0), the necessary argument is omitted. The stated reason for attainment is thus an invalid inference, and the correct reason has a gap.

failure_location.quote: the optima are attained and characterized as stationary points in $\Rnpp$. This is not obvious but follows since we have the ratios of convex and concave functions using $\lambda_{\max},\lambda_{\min}$ and this is over the open cone constraint $d\in\Rnpp$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pseudoconvexity-based attainment argument with the completed self-barrier argument: prove that as d approaches the boundary of {d: d^Te=n, d≥0}, the limit matrix D^{1/2}AD^{1/2} is rank-deficient (since D^{1/2} becomes singular), so by continuity of eigenvalues λ_min→0 and hence κ→∞; then invoke continuity of κ on the compact normalized slice to conclude attainment.
issues.overall_effect: The justification that the unconstrained problems (eq:optkappaprob) and (eq:probdDoforkappa) have solutions is unsupported as written. No formal theorem depends on this gap because the convergence analyses operate on the closed set Ω={d≥δe} where attainment follows from continuity and compactness of the normalized slice.
issues.title: Invalid inference from pseudoconvexity to attainment and unproved self-barrier claim in Remark Homogeneity
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local completion of the sketched self-barrier argument (a few lines showing rank-deficiency of the limit matrix) and removal of one invalid sentence. All substantive claims and guarantees survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: since \Cref{GD} is a subgradient method, in general it is not a descent method

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem first correctly states lim inf_{k→∞} κ(D̊(dₖ))=κ_* and then adds "in particular, κ(D̊(dₖ))↓κ_*", claiming the function values of the actual iterates converge monotonically to κ_*. Monotone convergence does not follow from lim inf convergence and is not provided by projected subgradient methods with diminishing stepsizes; the paper itself states that GD is "not a descent method". The correct consequence of lim inf=κ_* is that the running minimum κ_*^j=min_{k≤j}κ(D̊(dₖ)) (which the theorem defines but does not use in the conclusion) satisfies κ_*^j↓κ_*. The proof, citing Kiwiel's Theorem 1, establishes only best-iterate (or lim inf) convergence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the conclusion from "κ(D̊(dₖ))↓κ_*" to "κ_*^j↓κ_*", which correctly states that the best-iterate values decrease monotonically to κ_* and follows from lim inf=κ_*.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem overstates the convergence behavior of Algorithm GD by claiming monotone convergence of the iterates' function values. The meaningful convergence guarantee (best-iterate convergence to κ_*) is still established. No downstream result relies on the monotone convergence claim.
issues.title: Convergence theorem claims monotone convergence not provided by subgradient method
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single clause change in the theorem statement (replacing κ(D̊(dₖ)) with the already-defined κ_*^j). The convergence guarantee that the algorithm finds ε-optimal solutions is fully preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary claims the ω-optimal diagonal scaling is Jacobi (D=αDiag(diag(A))^{-1}) and that ∇ω(A)=0 iff A=αI. The proof says this "follows from the equality conditions in the harmonic-arithmetic mean inequalities," but the harmonic-arithmetic mean inequality (HM≤AM) is not the relevant result. The correct argument uses the AM-GM inequality on the products dᵢAᵢᵢ appearing in the trace of D^{1/2}AD^{1/2}, or alternatively the stationarity condition from thm:optomegacomp (diag(A)=(tr(A)/n)e implies dᵢAᵢᵢ=constant). The proof as written does not establish either claim: it cites the wrong inequality and provides no connecting argument. Both claims are correct and easily proved from the preceding theorem or AM-GM.

failure_location.quote:
This follows from the equality conditions in the harmonic-arithmetic mean
inequalities.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the "harmonic-arithmetic mean" argument with a correct AM-GM argument on the quantities dᵢAᵢᵢ appearing in ω(D^{1/2}AD^{1/2})=(ΣdᵢAᵢᵢ/n)/((∏dᵢ)det(A))^{1/n}, showing the lower bound (∏Aᵢᵢ/det(A))^{1/n} is attained iff all dᵢAᵢᵢ are equal (Jacobi scaling); and derive ∇ω(A)=0⟺A=αI directly from the gradient formula in thm:optomegacomp.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's two claims (Jacobi optimality and ∇ω(A)=0 characterization) are correct but unsupported by the given proof. The claims follow from the stationarity condition in thm:optomegacomp or from AM-GM on the diagonal entries.
issues.title: Proof of ω-optimal Jacobi scaling corollary invokes wrong inequality and is incomplete
issues.why_classification: The repair replaces one short incorrect inequality reference with a standard AM-GM argument (or a one-line deduction from the preceding theorem). All substantive claims and guarantees survive with no new lemma or construction.
